correctness.rationale: Two independent Python 3 certificate implementations checked all 14893 reverse-complement orbit subsets of sizes 0 through 6, using respectively Kahn elimination and DFS detection on all 32 graph states. They agree: no decycling sets of 0–5 orbits, exactly ten six-orbit decycling sets; length counts 6:4, 8:4, 10:2 and five complement-pairs. Rational recursion on the DAG establishes all ten expected hitting times, each independently re-evaluated from the explicit graph. The exhaustive finite scope and definitions are explicit; no extrapolation is made.

originality.rationale: The exact ten equality cases and their full shortest-window/mean-hit spectra are not implied by the published 2024 size-12 and one-witness longest-path-6 results. The 2003 foundations do not impose reversal-complement symmetry, and the 2026 parity theorem has no order-five equality classification. Targeted actual semantic research-record queries and primary literature comparisons yielded no dominating statement. The inaccessible 2024 supplement and unindexed equality enumerations remain concrete residual risks.
residual_risks: The 2024 paper provides a separately hosted supplement ZIP that was not accessible for inspection; a count of all optimizing codebooks there would potentially cover the claimed enumeration.
Unindexed author software or historic complete-search computations could contain the same ten equality cases.
The uniform random transition performance metric is not a realistic genome data statistic.

value.rationale: The new information classifies every optimum under a natural biologically motivated strand symmetry, quantifying three distinct sharp worst-case hitting windows at the already known minimum density and exactly five rational average-delay values. This is a complete equality-layer classification for a canonical small instance, useful for optimization benchmarks and selecting among optimal small sketching designs, without asserting a new capacity or realistic genome performance.
